# Open-Source Agent Attribution

NAAIL OpenLab™ may interoperate with or draw research inspiration from third-party open-source projects. Third-party code, trademarks, documentation, models, datasets, and research remain subject to their original rights and licenses.

## Registered projects

| Project | Upstream | License / status | NAAIL treatment |
|---|---|---|---|
| DSPy | https://github.com/stanfordnlp/dspy | MIT | Optional dependency / adapter boundary |
| STORM / Co-STORM | https://github.com/stanford-oval/storm | MIT | Optional dependency / adapter boundary |
| Hugging Face smolagents | https://github.com/huggingface/smolagents | Apache-2.0 | Optional dependency / executable swarm candidate |
| SceneSmith | https://github.com/nepfaff/scenesmith | MIT | Research inspiration unless separately integrated |
| Murakkab | https://news.mit.edu/2026/improving-ai-agent-speed-and-energy-efficiency-0625 | Research system; verify any released artifact separately | Research inspiration only by default |

## Rules

- Do not remove or replace upstream copyright/license notices.
- Do not present external code as NAAIL-owned code.
- Do not use university/company names or logos in a way that implies endorsement or affiliation.
- Record the exact dependency version or Git commit for reproducible empirical runs.
- Review licenses again before redistribution, marketplace publication, commercial use, or incorporation into a proprietary product.
- Review model and data terms separately from software-framework licenses.
- Keep confidential, licensed, restricted, or partner-provided data outside public examples and repositories.

NAAIL-specific professional-agent roles, synthetic Digital Twin designs, evaluation contracts, Evidence Passport™, Professional Decision DAG™, Human Gate controls, and educational protocols remain distinct from third-party frameworks even when an external library is used as an execution component.
